title: feat(runtime): POST /security/permission-sets/:name/clone, the permission-set clone door (#15204 stage CD)
body:
Part of #15204
Clause-②: yes (widening)

Stage CD of the #15194 epic: the permission-set clone door. The seat ruled it on objectui#7611 (Q1 → A, comment 6097763840) and the PM opened the stage in claim amendment 6111348289. Retiring `clone_permission_set` and `ActionParamSchema.carryOver` is stage 8's work and stays out of this PR. objectui PR-4 switches the console's Clone dispatch to this route after it lands.

## What lands

`POST /api/v1/security/permission-sets/:name/clone`, body `{ name, label }`.

- **Reads the source from the security catalog, never from a row.** It goes through the catalog reader the security plugin binds to the engine (`securityCatalogReaderOf`, registry first, then the metadata service), the same read `resolveUserAuthzGrants` uses. It reads no `sys_permission_set` row, so it works on a database that has none. The unit double throws on every data read, and the dogfood pin deletes the source's rows before it clones.
- **Writes the copy through the metadata door.** `protocol.saveMetaItem({ type: 'permission', name, item, parentVersion: null })` saves an environment-authored item with no organization and no package. `/meta`'s schema and its hooks judge the copy. The save does not keep the source's provenance off the copy: its authoring rule (`tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal`) judges `flow` writes only and answers null for `permission`, and its provenance strip is silent. The guarantee is `PERMISSION_SET_CLONE_DROPPED_KEYS` and the unit pin that asserts every dropped key absent from the saved item. `parentVersion: null` is the create-only pin (`If-None-Match: *`), so a row written under the target name after the catalog read is refused rather than overwritten.
- **Copies the whole definition and drops one server-declared list.** `PERMISSION_SET_CLONE_DROPPED_KEYS` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/permission-set-clone.ts`) holds:
  - the provenance envelope and read decorations, derived from the spec (`MetadataProtectionFields`, `METADATA_READ_DECORATIONS`);
  - `packageId`, `managedBy` and `protection`;
  - the two privilege decisions, `adminScope` and `isDefault`.
  Everything else crosses as a deep copy: `objects`, `fields`, `systemPermissions`, `tabPermissions`, `rowLevelSecurity` and `description`. No facet is enumerated, which follows ADR-0126 §7.1 ("never param-list assembly"). The response is `{ permissionSet, notice }`. It carries no ancestry (ADR-0126 §9), and the notice says what was not copied.
- **Authority is the metadata door's own.** The route asks the shared `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict` (`manage_metadata`, with `isSystem` bypassing) before any path, body or catalog read. This adds no gate and is not the ADR-0126 §5 activation gate (#22621 → A; four axes: a new gate is "no" by default).
- **Refusals use the ADR-0112 envelope:**
  - 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`: the caller lacks `manage_metadata`;
  - 401: anonymous, at the domain floor;
  - 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`: a name failing `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, at least 2 characters — the rule `PermissionSetSchema.name` uses, which the message states), or a body that is not exactly `{ name, label }`;
  - 404: an unknown source;
  - 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`: a name the catalog already holds, the source's own included;
  - 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`: no catalog is bound, or the catalog read fails;
  - 501: no metadata protocol is composed;
  - a failed save keeps the store's own status and code.

### Where it lives, and why

The path follows the flow precedent's family. `POST /automation/:name/clone` is an arm of the dispatcher's `/automation` domain, mounted by `dispatcher-plugin.ts` and ledgered `server-only` in `packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts`. The nearest sibling is `POST /security/_activation/:type/:name`, the one `/security` route the dispatcher already mounted, which reads the same catalog. So the clone arm sits in the dispatcher's `/security` domain (`domains/security.ts` → `domains/permission-set-clone.ts`) and is mounted beside the activation route. The route ledger gains a `server-only` row, with the activation row's note adjusted to say there are now two such routes. Following the flow row, the route gets no client SDK method: its caller is the Setup console, and adding a method later reclassifies the row to `sdk`. The plural `permission-sets` segment follows the REST naming rule. Nothing in `packages/rest` mounts anything under `/security/permission-sets` (the old discard-overlay route there is retired), so nothing collides.

The landing zone is `packages/runtime` rather than `packages/rest`. The measurement placed the producer family there: the REST server owns the rest of `/security`, but the flow clone and the catalog activation doors both live in the runtime dispatcher.

### Docs

- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`: a new section, "Cloning a permission set", and a pointer from the locked-base bullet.
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`: the `permission` row of the sanctioned-path table names the door.
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`: row 49 anchors the clone door's `manage_metadata` verdict. The census gate (`check:system-context-census`) found the new `isSystem` read site, and `gen:system-context-census` recomputed the counts.

## Tests

- `packages/runtime/src/domains/permission-set-clone.test.ts`, 16 cases, including:
  - the whole-definition copy, asserted by deep equality against the source minus the exported dropped list;
  - every dropped key absent from the copy;
  - the create-only save, with no organization or package;
  - no shared references between the copy and the catalog definition;
  - the authority ordering: a non-holder sending an unknown source and a bad body gets 403;
  - every refusal's status and code, with nothing saved.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/permission-set-clone-door.dogfood.test.ts`, 4 cases on a booted showcase:
  - a `manage_metadata` holder clones the packaged `showcase_field_ops_delegate` (it has `adminScope`) after its `sys_permission_set` rows are deleted, and the copy resolves through the catalog with no package, no `adminScope` and the source's `objects`;
  - `showcase_member_default` (`isDefault: true`) clones without `isDefault`, and a holder of a position naming the copy resolves the copy's grants;
  - 409, 404 and 400 over HTTP;
  - a signed-up member without `manage_metadata` gets 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, and nothing resolves under the attempted name.
- Ablation on a committed tree (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`): removing `'adminScope'` from `PERMISSION_SET_CLONE_DROPPED_KEYS` turned two unit cases red (2 failed / 14 passed). The restore left the blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty.

### Local verification

Measured on `6d4ffaea5` (the merge of `origin/main` at `6d5191e69`). The only commit after it, `2bc6c13c6`, recounts `system-context.mdx`.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: green, including `check:test-typecheck`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test`: 352 files passed; 5086 tests passed, 19 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test`, the full suite: 250 files passed, 1 skipped; 2017 tests passed, 9 skipped.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 115 commands derived. 113 were re-run on the merged head and all exit 0 after the census recount. The other two, `check:pm-dispatch-gates` (fast tier, 1828 cases) and `check:type-check-debt`, ran green on `9bfb9ebf8` before the merge. `--ran` reconciles 115 run and 0 not measured.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` over the touched TypeScript and script files: clean.

What the gates found during the run, and what fixed it:

- **`check:system-context-census`:** the new `isSystem` read site got a row 49 anchor. The counts were recomputed again after the merge, because `main` also added a site.
- **`check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`:** the body reader's `required` and `invalid_type` field codes are classified `foreign-vocabulary`, as the flow clone door's are.
- **`check:route-envelope`:** declares `permission-set-clone.ts` with `{ handBuilt: 0 }`.
- **`check:route-ledger-census`:** `--fix` recounted the runtime ledger sentence.
- **`check:engine-double-contract`:** the unit double dropped an unused `findOne`.
- **Dogfood `authz-conformance` / `authz-probe-blind-spot`:** the runtime ledger count moves 87 → 88 (main's inbound-hook row took 86 → 87 in the same window).

## Acceptance notes

- **The locked-base refusal prose still names the data-door clone.** `packaged-base-regime.ts` (`PACKAGED_BASE_REGIME.permission.routes.clone`) and `packaged-permission-set-lock.ts` say "the Clone action … or `POST /api/v1/data/sys_permission_set`". The stage-8 seat answer (#15204 comment 6110777865) assigns that prose to stage 8, so it is untouched here. The metadata-lifecycle docs row names the new door and says the refusal does not name it yet.
- `clone_permission_set` and `ActionParamSchema.carryOver` are unchanged; stage 8 retires them.
- The objectui half (PR-4, switching the console's Clone to this route) is not in this PR.
